title_en: Qian Zhongshu and People's Literature Publishing House v. Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House — copyright infringement dispute
keywords_en: civil; copyright dispute; first instance; intermediate people's court; Shanghai; Sichuan Province; natural person; legal person; General Principles of Civil Law; Copyright Law; whether collation constitutes infringement; protection period of exclusive publishing right; relationship between derivative work and original work; in favor of plaintiff; copyright infringement; exclusive publishing right; collation; book publishing; good faith; copyright; copyright dispute with Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House
full_text_en:
Qian Zhongshu and People's Literature Publishing House v. Xu Zhifen and
Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House — Copyright Infringement Dispute

Plaintiff: Qian Zhongshu, male, 86 years old, a cadre at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Agent ad litem: Lu Zhimin, lawyer of Beijing Zhongbei Law Firm.

Plaintiff: People's Literature Publishing House.
Legal Representative: Chen Zaochun, President.
Agent ad litem: Lu Zhimin, lawyer of Beijing Zhongbei Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Li Hao, copyright agent of Beijing Copyright Agency.

Defendant: Xu Zhifen, female, 40 years old, a cadre at Shanghai *Labor Daily*.
Agent ad litem: Zhu Miaochun and Zhou Jing, lawyers of Shanghai Jinmao Law Firm.

Defendant: Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House.
Legal Representative: Xiang Kexiao, President.
Agent ad litem: Zhu Miaochun, lawyer of Shanghai Jinmao Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Wang Sen, staff member of Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House.

The plaintiffs, Qian Zhongshu and People's Literature Publishing House, filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court against the defendants, Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House, over a copyright dispute.

Plaintiff Qian Zhongshu alleged: He is the copyright owner of the book *Fortress Besieged*. The two defendants, without the plaintiff's consent, collated and published *Fortress Besieged*, infringing on the plaintiff's right of adaptation and right of publication and use of *Fortress Besieged*. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the two defendants to cease the infringement, publicly apologize to the plaintiff in a national newspaper, and compensate for losses of RMB 88,320 based on 12% of the total retail price of the infringing publication.

Plaintiff People's Literature Publishing House alleged: Since 1980, it has continuously enjoyed the exclusive right to publish *Fortress Besieged*. This includes the original version in the same language and all subsequent revised editions and abridged versions. Any unauthorized reprint or publication of any version under a different guise constitutes an infringement on the plaintiff's exclusive right to publish. Within the period when both the copyright of *Fortress Besieged* and the exclusive right to publish were protected by law, defendant Xu Zhifen, without Qian Zhongshu's consent, collated *Fortress Besieged* and unauthorizedly authorized Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House to publish the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged*, thereby infringing on the plaintiff's exclusive right to publish the original work. Defendant Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House, knowing that Xu Zhifen had not obtained the right to collate *Fortress Besieged* from Qian Zhongshu, repeatedly reprinted and sold the infringing work, removed the words "collated edition" from the book cover, and used *Fortress Besieged* as the book title in book order forms sent nationwide, also infringing on the plaintiff's exclusive right to publish. The plaintiff requested the two defendants to cease the infringement, publicly apologize to the plaintiff in a national newspaper, and compensate for losses of RMB 220,400 based on 15% of the total retail price of the infringing publication.

Defendants Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House argued: The collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* collated and published by the defendants objectively infringed on the plaintiff Qian Zhongshu's right to use the work, and they were willing to publicly apologize to Qian Zhongshu and compensate for the losses caused thereby. *Fortress Besieged* was first published in a magazine. The base text used for the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* was the serialized novel published in *Renaissance* magazine. The collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* embodied the author's creative labor and had documentary and academic value, being a type of derivative work different from the original work *Fortress Besieged*. Since collation is a form of derivative use of an original work, the collated edition, as a derivative work, did not use the original version of the work published by plaintiff People's Literature Publishing House. Moreover, the date when People's Literature Publishing House obtained the exclusive right to publish should be calculated from the signing of the publishing contract with Qian Zhongshu on March 18, 1992. The defendants' use of the work before that date could not be subject to claims by People's Literature Publishing House. Therefore, the defendants did not infringe on the exclusive right to publish of People's Literature Publishing House.

The Shanghai Intermediate People's Court, after a public hearing, found the following facts: The novel *Fortress Besieged*, a full-length work created by plaintiff Qian Zhongshu over two years, was first published in the large-scale literary monthly *Renaissance* in Shanghai from February 1946 to January 1947, serialized in ten installments. In May 1947, the Shanghai Chenguang Publishing Company published the single-volume edition of *Fortress Besieged*, reprinted in September 1948, and reprinted again in March 1949. In November 1980, People's Literature Publishing House reset and published the work. During this period, Qian Zhongshu repeatedly made textual additions, deletions, and refinements to the work, making it more complete. From 1980 to July 1996, People's Literature Publishing House printed and distributed *Fortress Besieged* in 25 print runs, totaling over 1.34 million copies.

In 1980, plaintiff People's Literature Publishing House, with plaintiff Qian Zhongshu's consent, published *Fortress Besieged*. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Ministry of Culture's *Trial Regulations on Copyright Protection for Books and Periodicals*, People's Literature Publishing House exercised the exclusive right to publish *Fortress Besieged* until 1990. On February 4, 1991, Qian Zhongshu issued a written authorization to continue the publication of *Fortress Besieged* by People's Literature Publishing House, stating that a formal publishing contract would be signed in accordance with relevant national regulations after the *Copyright Law* came into effect. On March 18, 1992, Qian Zhongshu and People's Literature Publishing House signed a *Book Publishing Contract*, granting People's Literature Publishing House the exclusive right to continue publishing the Chinese text of *Fortress Besieged* in book form.

In 1990, defendant Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House commissioned defendant Xu Zhifen to collate the book *Fortress Besieged*. The base texts used by Xu Zhifen for the collation were the version serialized in *Renaissance* monthly from February 1946 to January 1947, the first edition published by Shanghai Chenguang Publishing Company in May 1947, and the reprint by People's Literature Publishing House in October 1980. When the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* was published, the full text of *Fortress Besieged* as serialized in *Renaissance* was typeset and published, with Xu Zhifen's collation notes attached to each page. From May 1991 to July 1992, Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House published and distributed a total of 120,000 copies of the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged*, including 10,000 hardcover copies priced at RMB 8.20 and 110,000 laminated copies priced at RMB 5.40 and RMB 6.20. Among the 120,000 copies of the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged*, 30,000 copies had the words "collated edition" on the cover, and 90,000 copies did not. In the order catalogs of the Sichuan Provincial Bookstore for the 5th National Book Fair sample viewing and ordering meeting and the 1992 Spring Xinhua Bookstore book sample viewing and ordering meeting, the listing for *Fortress Besieged* did not include the words "collated edition."

In June 1991, an editor from defendant Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House sent a copy of the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* to plaintiff Qian Zhongshu, hoping Qian Zhongshu would support the publication of the book. On July 23, plaintiff People's Literature Publishing House, on behalf of Qian Zhongshu, sent a letter to the Copyright Division of the Sichuan Provincial Press and Publication Bureau, requesting an investigation into the infringement of copyright and exclusive publishing rights by Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House. On August 8 of the same year, Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House, in letters to the Copyright Division of the Sichuan Provincial Press and Publication Bureau and the Editorial Office of People's Literature Publishing House, admitted that it had published and edited the book without obtaining Qian Zhongshu's consent, infringing on the author's rights, and that it had published the collated edition without first obtaining the consent of People's Literature Publishing House, unaware that Mr. Qian Zhongshu had granted the exclusive right to publish *Fortress Besieged* to People's Literature Publishing House, constituting an infringement. Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House also expressed willingness to apologize, compensate for losses, and ensure that such incidents would not recur. After August 1991, Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House continued to publish and distribute the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged*, totaling 80,000 copies, all of which had no words "collated edition" on the cover. In December, Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House remitted a manuscript fee of RMB 9,800 to Qian Zhongshu. In March 1992, Qian Zhongshu returned the above manuscript fee through the Beijing Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China. During this period, People's Literature Publishing House had numerous exchanges with Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House regarding the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged*.

The above facts were confirmed by the *Book Publishing Contract* signed between Qian Zhongshu and People's Literature Publishing House, correspondence between the plaintiffs and defendants, and statements of the parties, all on record.

The Shanghai Intermediate People's Court held that plaintiff Qian Zhongshu holds copyright over his novel *Fortress Besieged*. Defendant Xu Zhifen, without the copyright owner's consent, collated *Fortress Besieged*, and defendant Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House published the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged*. This conduct violated Articles 94 and 118 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China* and jointly constituted an infringement of Qian Zhongshu's copyright. Pursuant to Article 134, paragraph 1 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law*, they shall bear civil liability for cessation of infringement, compensation for losses, and apology. According to the agreement between the two plaintiffs in 1980 and relevant regulations, Qian Zhongshu's publication authorization letter of February 4, 1991, and the publication contract of March 18, 1992, People's Literature Publishing House lawfully held the exclusive right to publish *Fortress Besieged* from 1980 to March 2002. During this period, Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House's publication of *Fortress Besieged* under the name "collated edition," using the version originally published in *Renaissance* magazine together with Xu Zhifen's collation notes, was an inappropriate act of massively reproducing and distributing the book *Fortress Besieged*, violating the principle of good faith stipulated in Article 4 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law*, detrimental to the normal publishing order, and infringing on the exclusive right to publish the original work *Fortress Besieged* already held by People's Literature Publishing House. Accordingly, on December 9, 1994, the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

1. Defendants Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House shall bear liability for infringing plaintiff Qian Zhongshu's copyright, cease the infringement, and publicly apologize to plaintiff Qian Zhongshu in the *Guangming Daily* (the content of the written apology shall be subject to review by this court).
2. Defendants Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House shall jointly compensate plaintiff Qian Zhongshu RMB 88,320.
3. Defendants Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House shall bear liability for infringing plaintiff People's Literature Publishing House's exclusive right to publish, cease the infringement, and publicly apologize to plaintiff People's Literature Publishing House in the *Guangming Daily* (the content of the written apology shall be subject to review by this court).
4. Defendants Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House shall jointly compensate plaintiff People's Literature Publishing House RMB 110,400.
The case acceptance fee of RMB 5,140 shall be borne by the two defendants.

After the first-instance judgment, both defendants, Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House, appealed to the Shanghai High People's Court. The main grounds of appeal were: (1) The material facts found in the original judgment were unclear. The amount and time of the manuscript fee paid by Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House to Qian Zhongshu, and the time when Qian Zhongshu refused the fee, were unclear; the publishing contract signed on March 18, 1992, submitted by the two plaintiffs to the court, lacked sufficient basis and was difficult to identify as Qian Zhongshu's true intent; the original judgment's finding on the quantity of printed and published copies of the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* was unclear. (2) The characterization was improper. The original judgment confused the distinction between the first serialized version and the first single-volume edition. Without Qian Zhongshu's consent, collating and publishing the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* only infringed on Qian Zhongshu's right to collate and did not affect any other rights Qian Zhongshu had to use the work *Fortress Besieged*, let alone infringe on People's Literature Publishing House's exclusive right to publish. (3) The application of law was improper. The current *Copyright Law* of China stipulates that the exclusive right to publish is limited to "the original edition, revised edition, and abridged edition," and does not include a collated edition. The original judgment's citation of general principles of the *General Principles of the Civil Law* as the legal basis for finding infringement of the exclusive right to publish was clearly improper.

Upon further trial, the Shanghai High People's Court identified the following main issues with the first-instance findings of facts: (1) The finding that appellant Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House published and distributed 10,000 copies of the hardcover collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* at a price of RMB 8.20 was erroneous. Upon review, it was found that Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House published and distributed a total of 10,000 hardcover copies of the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged*, of which 5,000 copies were published in May 1991 at a price of RMB 7.40, and 5,000 copies were published in March 1992 at a price of RMB 8.20. Therefore, the first-instance judgment erred in determining the price for 5,000 copies of the hardcover collated edition. (2) The finding on the time and amount of the remittance from Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House to Qian Zhongshu was erroneous. The first-instance judgment found that in December 1991, Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House remitted a manuscript fee of RMB 9,800 to Qian Zhongshu, which was refused. Upon review, it was found that on October 1991, Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House remitted a manuscript fee of RMB 974.02 for the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* to Qian Zhongshu through the Chengdu Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China. Qian Zhongshu returned the money in March 1992, as indicated in the special transfer receipt of the Beijing Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, which noted "payee refused, therefore returned." (3) Due to the erroneous determination of the price of the hardcover collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* in the first instance, the calculation of the compensation amount was erroneous. The compensation to Qian Zhongshu was overcalculated by RMB 480, and the compensation to People's Literature Publishing House was overcalculated by RMB 600.

The Shanghai High People's Court held: According to Articles 10 and 12 of the *Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China*, copyright includes the rights of publication, authorship, alteration, integrity, use, and remuneration. The copyright in derivative works created by adaptation, translation, annotation, or arrangement of preexisting works shall be enjoyed by the adapters, translators, annotators, or arrangers, but the exercise of such copyright shall not infringe on the copyright in the original works. Accordingly, Qian Zhongshu lawfully enjoys the copyright in the book *Fortress Besieged*. "Collation" is a form of deriving from an original work. The collator must collate in accordance with the law and shall not infringe on the copyright in the original work. Xu Zhifen, without Qian Zhongshu's permission, collated *Fortress Besieged*, infringing on Qian Zhongshu's right to use the work and right to remuneration. Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House, for profit, published and distributed the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* when Qian Zhongshu had not authorized anyone to collate the work, thereby also constituting an infringement on Qian Zhongshu's copyright and shall bear joint liability. Before the formal implementation of the *Copyright Law*, relevant documents of the Ministry of Culture and the Copyright Bureau stipulated that when an author or other copyright owner transfers the publishing right of a work to a domestic publishing unit, it shall be an exclusive publishing right (i.e., the right to publish the original, revised, excerpted, and selected editions, and the right to reprint). A domestic publisher enjoys the right to publish the book it has published based on an agreement between the author and the compiler/annotator. Without authorization from the original publisher, other publishers have no right to reprint, nor may they arbitrarily delete (excluding abridged versions) or republish under a different guise. After the *Copyright Law* came into effect, it clearly provides that: "A book publisher shall enjoy the exclusive right to publish the work delivered by the copyright owner within the contractually agreed period. The period for which a book publisher is granted the exclusive right to publish by contract shall not exceed ten years and may be renewed upon expiration. The exclusive right to publish enjoyed by a book publisher within the contractually agreed period is protected by law, and no other party may publish the work." The exclusive right to publish Qian Zhongshu's work *Fortress Besieged* enjoyed by People's Literature Publishing House is protected by law. Without permission, no other party may publish the work. Shortly after Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House published the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* in May 1991, it received objections from Qian Zhongshu and People's Literature Publishing House. At that time, the publishing house admitted that its conduct constituted an infringement, claiming to have published the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* purely by mistake, and expressed willingness to apologize and compensate for losses. However, after August 1991, it continued to publish a large number of copies of the collated edition of *Fortress Besieged*, as many as 80,000 copies. Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House also removed the words "collated edition" from the order forms and the covers of 90,000 copies of the officially published collated edition of *Fortress Besieged*, while printing the words "collated edition" on another 30,000 copies. These actions during the publication and distribution process sufficiently indicate that the publishing house was publishing *Fortress Besieged* in the form of a collated edition. Such conduct has violated the principles of good faith and respect for social morality, disrupted normal publishing order, and constituted an infringement on the exclusive right to publish of People's Literature Publishing House. The two appellants shall bear civil liability for cessation of infringement, apology, and compensation for losses in accordance with Article 45, item (5) and Article 46, item (3) of the *Copyright Law*. The first-instance court's findings on the main facts of the case were generally clear, but the determination of the price for part of the hardcover collated edition of *Fortress Besieged* was erroneous and shall be corrected. The *General Principles of the Civil Law* are the guidelines for regulating civil conduct in our country. The first-instance court's application of the provisions of the *General Principles of the Civil Law* regarding copyright to render the judgment was not improper. Since the *Copyright Law* came into effect in our country on June 1, 1991, applying the specialized law to adjudicate copyright infringements that occurred after its implementation is more appropriate. The other grounds of appeal of the appellants are untenable and shall be dismissed. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 153, items (1) and (3) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, the Shanghai High People's Court rendered the following judgment on December 25, 1996:

1. Affirm item (1) of the first-instance civil judgment.
2. Amend item (2) of the first-instance civil judgment to: Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House shall jointly compensate Qian Zhongshu for losses in the amount of RMB 87,840.
3. Affirm item (3) of the first-instance civil judgment.
4. Amend item (4) of the first-instance civil judgment to: Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House shall jointly compensate People's Literature Publishing House for losses in the amount of RMB 109,800.
The litigation costs of the first and second instances, totaling RMB 10,924, shall be borne by Xu Zhifen and Sichuan Literature and Art Publishing House.
